clue.text: Accept a token in new deal

indicators.note: a fresh deal of the cards reshuffles them, so the letters of these words are dealt out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at a card table agrees to put a token into the pot for the next hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a challenge or task is to undertake it, a common phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Time young birds may be found in straw etc

parts.note: a hatch is a brood of newly hatched chicks

explanation.surface: It is the season when chicks may be found nesting in the straw and similar stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be found in' is only a link to the definition, though it pretends the birds are inside the straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofing material made of straw, reeds and similar dried plant stalks is the classic example.

clue.text: Tricky mile trek including middle of bog? A shorter distance

indicators.note: including means the anagrammed letters take in the next piece
something tricky is twisted or awkward, signalling that the letters of mile trek are scrambled
the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A hike across a boggy mile is awkward, so perhaps a shorter route is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' rearranges MILE TREK, and 'including' puts O, from 'middle of bog', among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of length is about five-eighths of a mile, so it is a shorter distance.

clue.text: What was paid off long ago in coppers?

definitions.text: What was paid off long ago
definitions.meaning: an account settled years back is an old debt, read literally
British slang for the police as a body

explanation.surface: A question about some debt from long ago, settled in copper coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like pennies, which fits paying off a debt, but here means police officers. OLD BILL is everyday British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers are known in British slang by this name; literally it is an ancient invoice.

clue.text: Little reptile exploits flowering plants

parts.note: croc is the short form of crocodile
to exploit something is to use it

explanation.surface: A small reptile makes use of some flowering plants for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: These are spring-flowering bulbs of the iris family, so they are plants that flower.

clue.text: Girl given payment in beastly home, brought up to be respectful

indicators.note: in places the girl and payment inside the turned den
in a down entry, bringing a word up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a lair is a wild animal's den
Eve is a girl's name
rent is a regular payment for lodging

explanation.surface: A girl paid to live in a dreadful home was nonetheless raised to show respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' acts only on the den, which then holds the girl and the payment. 'beastly' looks like 'horrible' but means belonging to a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep respect or reverence, as in a reverent manner, is the meaning.

clue.text: Business of transporting stuff — hard to get out of old African capital

indicators.note: says the letter for hard is to leave the ancient city's name

parts.note: Carthage was the ancient capital of a North African empire
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A haulage firm finds it hard to get out of an ancient African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Conveying goods by cart or truck, and the charge for it, is what the word means.

clue.text: Number in double figures to achieve success

definitions.meaning: twenty is a two-digit number, and a set of twenty has this name
to have a hit or win, as in a goal or a deal

explanation.surface: Reaching a two-figure tally is what it takes to succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a set of twenty; the verb means to win a point or have a success.

clue.text: Attend match, say, in which muscle is evident

indicators.note: in which shows the muscle sitting inside the word for say

parts.note: to state is to say
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: Turning up to a match, say, where some player's muscles are on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match, say' reads as one phrase, but the comma splits them: 'match' ends the definition and 'say' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch an event such as a game as a member of the crowd is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Make reference, as man getting audibly vulgar

parts.note: acting as one man means all together

indicators.note: audibly means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: lewd means crude or vulgar; said straight after the word for everyone, its L merges into the preceding double L, leaving the sound ude

explanation.surface: As a man, he becomes noticeably coarse in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' works on the whole phrase: said aloud, 'all lewd' runs together as the answer, the two L sounds merging into one.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to something indirectly is the verb's meaning, a near synonym.

clue.text: Always you must keep on — not just some of you!

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever-hopeful

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the old word for you holds on

parts.note: ye is the archaic plural form of you

explanation.surface: A rallying cry: you must keep going, every last one of you.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means all people, the opposite of only some.

clue.text: As Soviet official, I'm cross, am mad

indicators.note: the letters go mad, scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Soviet functionary declares himself cross and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A Communist Party official in charge of political education was the title in Soviet Russia.

clue.text: Economy good with people showing a redeeming quality

parts.note: saving money is economy
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Thrift together with decent people shows a single virtue that redeems a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A single good trait that makes up for other faults is exactly a redeeming quality.

clue.text: Excellent department led by ace

indicators.note: led by puts the letter for ace at the front

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A top-notch department headed by a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being highly skilled at something, an expert, is the meaning; synonym.

clue.text: A live gent's let loose, a gospel preacher

indicators.note: let loose, the letters are freed to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lively gentleman, released, becomes a preacher of the gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' belongs to the fodder, not to the indicator, though 'let loose' reads as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an evangelist who preaches on television, so a gospel preacher by example.

clue.text: Alien gent, frightfully lacking in refinement

indicators.note: frightfully suggests something done in a terrible, disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial gentleman is terribly unpolished.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or style is what the adjective means, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Harry and Edward tinkered about

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of the novels
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named Harry and Edward fiddled around.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to busy oneself idly with small tasks, the same as tinkering.

clue.text: Doctor on visit — severe and a bit too touchy?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor on a house call is harsh and rather prickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easily hurt or offended to excess is excessive touchiness, a synonym.

clue.text: The female subsequently lacking a sanctuary

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: lacking says the letter a is missing from the word for subsequently

parts.note: later means subsequently

explanation.surface: The woman later found herself without a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of refuge or protection, a synonym for sanctuary.

clue.text: One thus tardy is to get set apart from others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so means thus
late means tardy

explanation.surface: Someone who is so late gets kept apart from everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate something or someone from others, as in quarantine, is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Oriental dropping off at the front gets behind

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: eastern means oriental
the letter dropped is the opening E of the word for Oriental

explanation.surface: An Eastern traveller, falling asleep up front, ends up at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' suggests nodding off, but means losing a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical word meaning at or toward the rear of a ship, so behind.

clue.text: Cardinal providing article about Religious Education

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article surrounds the next piece

parts.note: the is the definite article
RE is the school-subject abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cardinal writes an article on religious education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman but means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal number is a counting number such as one, two, or this one.

clue.text: Frolics of old politicians undermining Speaker ultimately

indicators.note: in a down entry, undermining means placed beneath
ultimately points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Antics of former politicians that undercut the Commons Speaker in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively, boisterous play is the meaning, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Bitterness showing by those with aspiration heading off, quick movers

parts.note: gall is bitterness or resentment

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: people who aspire are hopers

explanation.surface: Resentment is shown by ambitious people setting off, like fast runners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' also hints at the aspirated H, which is the letter lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses that run at full gait are fast-moving creatures, hence quick movers.

clue.text: Have a hand in genuine action to cancel debt?

indicators.note: in places the hand inside the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A genuine hand at work in getting debts written off.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission, the act of releasing a debt or penalty, is what the word names.

clue.text: One form of music and another making comeback with time

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: rag, as in ragtime, is another form of music
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: One musical style and another stage a revival over time.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genre of electronic dance music, an example of a musical form.

clue.text: Rat in dry zone here shedding skin

parts.note: a desert is an arid area

indicators.note: shedding skin means losing the outer letters

explanation.surface: A rodent in an arid region sheds its skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal but is a verb-turned-noun: someone who abandons a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for a turncoat who abandons allies, synonym for one who runs away.

clue.text: 1 Across funny old comedian

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the solution to the clue at 1 Across

explanation.surface: A cross-reference describes a comic of yesteryear.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was a silent-film comic of the 1920s, an example.
